newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan reports hog foot and mouth disease outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan reports hog foot and mouth disease outbreak.

text.p: Taiwan's Council of Agriculture on Thursday announced an outbreak of the highly contagious foot and mouth disease in its hog population, saying this would jeopardise the island's large pork exports.
"Laboratory tests have determined that a disease found in the hog population is indeed foot and mouth disease," an official of the cabinet agency told Reuters by telephone.
A statement issued by the council said all exports of fresh and frozen pork would be banned temporarily.

Japan, which is Taiwan's largest pork export market, has strict rules against importation of pork from regions known to be affected by hog foot and mouth disease and was expected to impose its own ban on shipments from Taiwan, experts said.

Japan has been importing some 16,000 tonnes of fresh and frozen pork from Taiwan a month despite Tokyo's imposition of a special "emergency" import tariff to limit imports and protect local breeders. Taiwan's pork exports to Japan alone comprise about 69 percent of the island's total pork exports.
The Taiwan council said instances of highly contagious foot and mouth disease had been found in nine Taiwan counties and more than 20 breeding farms.
"This is an airborne disease that has a very high tolerance to sanitation measures," the council said in a statement. "The death rate is very high."

The Taiwan council estimated that Taiwan breeds 14 million hogs per year. According to a 1994 survey, the industry was worth T$89 billion (US$3.24 billion), or about 20 percent of Taiwan's farm market and 60 percent of the livestock sector.
Taiwan's pork industry employs 700,000 people, including 100,000 pig farmers, the council said.
